## Replication with new data {#replication-with-new-data .smaller}

::: {.small}
- A replication asks **the same question of new data**: here, later waves of the Standard Eurobarometer, which kept asking what the EU means to people
- The SCORE replicability study ran one: fourteen Standard waves fielded between 2013 and 2019, in the member states and the United Kingdom
- Its verdict: a **positive** coefficient for unemployment, not significant, so the replication was **not successful** by the criterion of SCORE
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
A failed replication says that the claim did not hold in those data with that analysis. On its own it cannot say whether the data, the analysis or the world had changed.
:::

::: notes
The last of the three Rs is replication, the same question asked of new data. For this claim the new data exist, because the Standard Eurobarometer kept asking people what the EU means to them after the original study ended in 2013. The SCORE replicability study took fourteen Standard waves fielded between 2013 and 2019, in the member states and the United Kingdom, and fitted a model close to that of the original author. It found a positive coefficient for unemployment, the opposite sign to the claim, and not significant, so the replication was not successful by the criterion that SCORE had set. [advance] That verdict says that the claim did not hold in those data with that analysis, and on its own it cannot say which of the three changed: the data, the analysis or a relationship that may have shifted over a decade.
:::

## Decisions to fix in advance {#decisions-to-fix-in-advance .smaller}

::: {.small}
| Decision | For a replication of your analysis |
|:--|:--|
| **The claim and its test** | which coefficient, which sign, which threshold counts as success |
| **The data** | which waves, which countries, which unemployment series |
| **The measurement** | the fifteenth answer category that the list has carried since the end of 2019, the respondents who mention nothing |
| **The analysis** | the model of your analyst, as you reproduced it, unchanged |
| **The report** | what you will say if the result differs, and what if it agrees |
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
All five can be fixed **before the new data are opened**, which is what a preregistration is for.
:::

::: notes
A replication of the analysis that you reproduced earlier involves decisions of five kinds, and every one of them can be taken before you open the new data. The first is the coefficient that you will read, the sign that the claim predicts and the threshold that counts as success, and the second the waves, the countries and the unemployment series, given that the series that you reproduced may have been revised since. The third is measurement, the fifteenth answer category, the quality of life of future generations, which the list has carried since the end of 2019 and which changes the denominator of every share of mentions, and the respondents who mention nothing. The model is naturally the one that you reproduced, unchanged, which is what makes the work a replication rather than a new analysis, and the last decision is what you will say whichever way the result comes out. [advance] Fixing these decisions in advance is what a preregistration does, and it is the last task of the day.
:::
